ARCHIVE - Greenstreets.query: Using the Greenstreets dataset, could you categorize greenstreets by size based on their length ('Small Greenstreet' ≤300, 'Medium Greenstreet' 301–800, 'Large Greenstreet' >800)? For each size category, grouped by borough, department, greenstreet type, contract, and description, please show the count, average length, total length, and maximum length.
ARCHIVE - Greenstreets.sql:
WITH categorized_data AS (
  SELECT
    t1.system,
    t3.system,
    t1.department,
    t1.communityb,
    t1.class,
    t1.gsgroup,
    t1.parentorg,
    t3.nys_senate,
    t3.status,
    t3.commission,
    t5.borough,
    t5.gstype,
    t5.location,
    t5.precinct,
    t5.shape_stle,
    CASE
      WHEN t5.shape_stle > 800 THEN 'Large Greenstreet'
      WHEN t5.shape_stle > 300 THEN 'Medium Greenstreet'
      ELSE 'Small Greenstreet'
    END as category,
    t2.contract,
    t4.descriptio
  FROM "ARCHIVE - Greenstreets_greenstreets_site_information" t1
  INNER JOIN "node_2" t2
    ON t1.objectid = t2.objectid
  INNER JOIN "ARCHIVE - Greenstreets_greenstreets_senate_commissions" t3
    ON t1.system = t3.system
  INNER JOIN "ARCHIVE - Greenstreets_greenstreets_park_locations" t4
    ON t2.omppropid = t4.omppropid
  INNER JOIN "ARCHIVE - Greenstreets_greenstreets_locations_nyc" t5
    ON t4.global_id = t5.global_id
  WHERE t5.gstype IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT
  borough,
  department,
  gstype,
  category,
  COUNT(*) as count,
  AVG(shape_stle) as avg_value,
  SUM(shape_stle) as total_value,
  MAX(shape_stle) as max_value
FROM categorized_data
GROUP BY
  borough,
  department,
  gstype,
  category, contract, descriptio

2019 Pre-Kindergarten Admissions Guide.query: Using the 2019 Pre-Kindergarten Admissions Guide data, for each geographic district, could you show me the top 7 programs ranked by the number of additional priorities they offer? For each program, please include the address, geographic district, program type, dual language programs, language support programs, early learn seats, non-sibling offers, neighborhood tabulation area, community board, extended hours availability for all schools, additional priorities, and out-of-district PK-only offers. Also include a separate ranking showing how each program compares within its neighborhood area based on early learn seat capacity using dense rank.
2019 Pre-Kindergarten Admissions Guide.sql:
WITH ranked AS (
  SELECT
    t4.address,
    t5.address,
    t3.geodistrict,
    t3.programtype,
    t3.duallanguageprograms,
    t4.languagesupportprograms,
    t3.earlylearnseats,
    t3.nonsiblingoffers,
    t5.nta,
    t5.community_board,
    t5.extendedhoursallschools,
    t5.additionalpriorities,
    t5.outofdistrictofferspkconly,
    RANK() OVER (
      PARTITION BY t3.geodistrict
      ORDER BY t5.additionalpriorities DESC
    ) as rank,
    DENSE_RANK() OVER (
      PARTITION BY t5.nta
      ORDER BY t3.earlylearnseats
    ) as dense_rank,
    t1.geodistrict,
    t2.languagesupports
  FROM "2019 Pre-Kindergarten Admissions Guide_pre_k_admissions_data" t1
  INNER JOIN "2019 Pre-Kindergarten Admissions Guide_pre_k_admissions_manhattan" t2
    ON t1.dbn = t2.dbn
  INNER JOIN "2019 Pre-Kindergarten Admissions Guide_pre_k_admissions_data" t3
    ON t1.programname = t3.programname
  INNER JOIN "2019 Pre-Kindergarten Admissions Guide_pre_k_school_contact_info" t4
    ON t2.phonenumber = t4.phonenumber
  INNER JOIN "node_5" t5
    ON t4.address = t5.address
  WHERE t3.earlylearnseats IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT
  address,
  geodistrict,
  programtype,
  duallanguageprograms,
  languagesupportprograms,
  earlylearnseats,
  nonsiblingoffers,
  nta,
  community_board,
  extendedhoursallschools,
  additionalpriorities,
  outofdistrictofferspkconly,
  rank,
  dense_rank
FROM ranked
WHERE rank <= 7

NYC Clean Heat Dataset (Historical).query: Using the NYC Clean Heat Dataset, could you identify the top 4 buildings with the highest fuel consumption in each neighborhood (NTA)? For each building, I would like to see the building manager, location details (borough, block and lot, NTA), building characteristics (total units, residential units, number of floors, year built), boiler information (installation date, capacity, utility type), and the total fuel consumption in gallons.
NYC Clean Heat Dataset (Historical).sql:
WITH ranked_data AS (
  SELECT
    t1.building_manager,
    t3.building_manager,
    t4.borough_block_lot,
    t5.borough_block_lot,
    t3.borough,
    t5.nta,
    t3.total_units,
    t3.boiler_installation_date,
    t4.year_built,
    t4.utility,
    t4.boiler_capacity_gross_btu,
    t5.of_res_units,
    t5.of_floors,
    t1.total_gallons_high,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
      PARTITION BY t5.nta
      ORDER BY t1.total_gallons_high DESC
    ) as row_num,
    t2.boiler_age_range
  FROM "NYC Clean Heat Dataset (Historical)_boiler_fuel_usage_records" t1
  INNER JOIN "NYC Clean Heat Dataset (Historical)_nyc_boiler_compliance_data" t2
    ON t1.dep_boiler_application = t2.dep_boiler_application
  INNER JOIN "node_3" t3
    ON t1.building_manager = t3.building_manager
  INNER JOIN "NYC Clean Heat Dataset (Historical)_nyc_building_heating_data" t4
    ON t2.owner = t4.owner
  INNER JOIN "NYC Clean Heat Dataset (Historical)_nyc_building_ownership_info" t5
    ON t4.borough_block_lot = t5.borough_block_lot
  WHERE t1.total_gallons_high IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT
  building_manager,
  borough_block_lot,
  borough,
  nta,
  total_units,
  boiler_installation_date,
  year_built,
  utility,
  boiler_capacity_gross_btu,
  of_res_units,
  of_floors,
  total_gallons_high
FROM ranked_data
WHERE row_num <= 4

2020 DOE High School Directory.query: Using the 2020 DOE High School Directory, could you categorize schools by their Grade 9 applicant volume into 'Very High Applicant Volume' (>1500 applicants), 'High Applicant Volume' (801-1500 applicants), and 'Typical Applicant Volume' (≤800 applicants)? For each category, grouped by borough, admission method, ELL programs offered, and eligibility3, please show the count of schools, average number of applicants, total applicants, and maximum applicants.
2020 DOE High School Directory.sql:
WITH categorized_data AS (
  SELECT
    t2.code1,
    t4.code1,
    t4.fax_number,
    t5.fax_number,
    t3.borough,
    t5.method1,
    t5.ell_programs,
    t4.grade9geapplicants1,
    t5.total_students,
    t5.graduation_rate,
    t2.finalgrades,
    t2.city,
    CASE
      WHEN t4.grade9geapplicants1 > 1500 THEN 'Very High Applicant Volume'
      WHEN t4.grade9geapplicants1 > 800 THEN 'High Applicant Volume'
      ELSE 'Typical Applicant Volume'
    END as category,
    t1.eligibility3
  FROM "node_1" t1
  INNER JOIN "2020 DOE High School Directory_high_school_admissions_data" t2
    ON t1.dbn = t2.dbn
  INNER JOIN "2020 DOE High School Directory_nyc_high_school_directory" t3
    ON t1.school_name = t3.school_name
  INNER JOIN "2020 DOE High School Directory_high_school_programs_info" t4
    ON t2.code1 = t4.code1
  INNER JOIN "2020 DOE High School Directory_high_school_admissions_data_1" t5
    ON t4.fax_number = t5.fax_number
  WHERE t4.grade9geapplicants1 IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT
  borough,
  method1,
  ell_programs,
  category,
  COUNT(*) as count,
  AVG(grade9geapplicants1) as avg_value,
  SUM(grade9geapplicants1) as total_value,
  MAX(grade9geapplicants1) as max_value
FROM categorized_data
GROUP BY
  borough,
  method1,
  ell_programs,
  category, eligibility3

NYC Free Tax Prep Sites.query: Using the NYC Free Tax Prep Sites data, could you please show me the top 4 tax preparation sites in each borough that are listed in the 311 system, ranked by their easternmost location (highest X coordinate)? I'd like to see the provider name, borough, opening date, s1, income limit, website, street, unit, service notes, mapped address, amended return status, X coordinate, l1, and Monday closing time for each site.
NYC Free Tax Prep Sites.sql:
WITH ranked_data AS (
  SELECT
    t3.providername,
    t3.borough,
    t3.opendateiso,
    t3.s1,
    t3.incomelimit,
    t3.website,
    t3.street,
    t3.unit,
    t3.notes,
    t5.mappedaddress,
    t5.show311,
    t5.amendedreturn,
    t5.xcoordinate,
    t5.l1,
    t5.mondayclose,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
      PARTITION BY t3.borough
      ORDER BY t5.xcoordinate DESC
    ) as row_num,
    t1.apptorwalkin,
    t2.longitude,
    t4.longitude
  FROM "NYC Free Tax Prep Sites_nyc_tax_prep_sites_1" t1
  INNER JOIN "NYC Free Tax Prep Sites_nyc_tax_prep_locations_2" t2 ON t1.sitekey = t2.sitekey
  INNER JOIN "NYC Free Tax Prep Sites_nyc_tax_prep_sites" t3 ON t1.sitename = t3.sitename
  INNER JOIN "NYC Free Tax Prep Sites_nyc_tax_prep_locations" t4 ON t2.latitude = t4.latitude AND t2.longitude = t4.longitude
  INNER JOIN "NYC Free Tax Prep Sites_nyc_tax_prep_locations_1" t5 ON t4.building = t5.building
  WHERE t5.show311 = 'Yes'
)
SELECT
  providername,
  borough,
  opendateiso,
  s1,
  incomelimit,
  website,
  street,
  unit,
  notes,
  mappedaddress,
  amendedreturn,
  xcoordinate,
  l1,
  mondayclose
FROM ranked_data
WHERE row_num <= 4

NYC Free Tax Prep Sites.query: Show, for each building in the NYC Free Tax Prep Sites data, the three most recent records based on the open date, including the main site identifier, the open date, the building, whether they provide individual taxpayer identification number services, the first-level location or unit, and the full mapped address, along with the ranking within each building, the dense ranking within each individual taxpayer identification number group, whether appointments or walk-ins are accepted, and the longitude.
NYC Free Tax Prep Sites.sql:
WITH ranked AS (
  SELECT 
    t3.s1,
    t3.opendateiso,
    t4.building,
    t4.itin,
    t5.building,
    t5.l1,
    t5.mappedaddress,
    RANK() OVER (
      PARTITION BY t5.building 
      ORDER BY t3.opendateiso DESC

  FROM `NYC Free Tax Prep Sites_nyc_tax_prep_sites_1` t1
  INNER JOIN `NYC Free Tax Prep Sites_nyc_tax_prep_locations_2` t2 ON t1.sitekey = t2.sitekey

  INNER JOIN `NYC Free Tax Prep Sites_nyc_tax_prep_locations_1` t5 ON t4.building = t5.building
)
SELECT 
  s1,
  opendateiso,
  building,
  itin,
  l1,
  mappedaddress,
  rank,
  dense_rank, apptorwalkin, longitude
FROM ranked
WHERE rank <= 3

NYC Free Tax Prep Sites.query: Could you list the top 50 free tax prep locations with the highest combined activity or usage score, showing for each one the site’s name, where it’s located (including its street or building info and general area), and the coordinates you have for it, along with how many matching records you found there, the total of that usage score, and the average value per record?
NYC Free Tax Prep Sites.sql:
WITH base_data AS (
  SELECT 
    t1.sitename,
    t1.sitekey,
    t2.sitekey AS t2_sitekey,
    t2.latitude,
    t2.longitude,
    t3.sitename AS t3_sitename,
    t3.s1,
    t4.latitude AS t4_latitude,
    t4.longitude AS t4_longitude,
    t4.building AS t4_building,
    t5.building,
    t5.l1,
    t5.xcoordinate
  FROM `NYC Free Tax Prep Sites_nyc_tax_prep_sites_1` t1
  INNER JOIN `NYC Free Tax Prep Sites_nyc_tax_prep_locations_2` t2 ON t1.sitekey = t2.sitekey
  INNER JOIN `NYC Free Tax Prep Sites_nyc_tax_prep_sites` t3 ON t1.sitename = t3.sitename
  INNER JOIN `NYC Free Tax Prep Sites_nyc_tax_prep_locations` t4 ON t2.latitude = t4.latitude AND t2.longitude = t4.longitude
  INNER JOIN `NYC Free Tax Prep Sites_nyc_tax_prep_locations_1` t5 ON t4.building = t5.building
  WHERE t3.s1 IS NOT NULL
), aggregated AS (
  SELECT 
    sitename,
    latitude,
    longitude,
    building,
    l1,
    SUM(xcoordinate) AS total,
    COUNT(*) AS count,
    AVG(xcoordinate) AS average
  FROM base_data
  GROUP BY sitename, latitude, longitude, building, l1
)
SELECT 
  sitename,
  latitude,
  longitude,
  building,
  l1,
  total,
  count,
  average
FROM aggregated
WHERE count >= 1
ORDER BY total DESC
LIMIT 50

LinkNYC Kiosk Status (Historical).query: Using the LinkNYC Kiosk Status (Historical) data, could you analyze the kiosk service status by breaking it down by borough, WiFi status, and tablet status? For each combination that has more than one kiosk, please show the total council district values, the count of kiosks, the average council district number, and the longitude, ordered by the total council district value.
LinkNYC Kiosk Status (Historical).sql:
WITH base_data AS (
  SELECT
    t1.site_id,
    t3.site_id,
    t1.ppt_id,
    t4.ppt_id,
    t1.wifi_status,
    t1.phone_status,
    t1.cross_street_1,
    t1.council_district,
    t3.city,
    t3.bbl,
    t4.tablet_status,
    t4.status,
    t4.install_date,
    t4.community_board,
    t5.nta,
    t5.generated_on,
    t5.wifi_status_date,
    t6.boro,
    t6.corner,
    t2.longitude
  FROM "LinkNYC Kiosk Status (Historical)_linknyc_kiosk_status_history" t1
  INNER JOIN "LinkNYC Kiosk Status (Historical)_linknyc_kiosk_locations_2" t2 ON t1.unique_id = t2.unique_id
  INNER JOIN "LinkNYC Kiosk Status (Historical)_linknyc_kiosk_locations_1" t3 ON t1.site_id = t3.site_id
  INNER JOIN "node_4" t4 ON t1.ppt_id = t4.ppt_id
  INNER JOIN "LinkNYC Kiosk Status (Historical)_linknyc_kiosk_status_history_1" t5 ON t2.latitude = t5.latitude AND t2.longitude = t5.longitude
  INNER JOIN "LinkNYC Kiosk Status (Historical)_linknyc_kiosk_locations" t6 ON t2.address = t6.address
  WHERE t1.council_district IS NOT NULL
),
aggregated AS (
  SELECT
    boro,
    wifi_status,
    tablet_status,
    SUM(TRY_CAST(council_district AS DOUBLE)) as total,
    COUNT(*) as count,
    AVG(TRY_CAST(council_district AS DOUBLE)) as average,
    longitude
  FROM base_data
  GROUP BY
    boro,
    wifi_status,
    tablet_status, longitude
)
SELECT
  boro,
  wifi_status,
  tablet_status,
  total,
  count,
  average,
  longitude
FROM aggregated
WHERE count > 1
ORDER BY total DESC
LIMIT 80

Bikes in Buildings Requests.query: Using the Bikes in Buildings Requests data, could you categorize bike parking requests by council district into 'Lower-numbered district' (≤10), 'Mid-numbered district' (11-20), and 'Upper-numbered district' (>20)? For each category, grouped by neighborhood (NTA), service type (self-service or operator), tenant city, and owner city, please show the count of requests along with the average, total, and maximum council district numbers.
Bikes in Buildings Requests.sql:
WITH categorized_data AS (
  SELECT
    t1.indexnumber,
    t3.indexnumber,
    t1.tenantname,
    t4.tenantname,
    t1.tenantcity,
    t1.tenantfloor,
    t3.selfserviceoroperator,
    t3.plansubmitdate,
    t4.nta,
    t4.council_district,
    t4.routetoalternateparking,
    t5.tenantstreetname,
    t5.census_tract,
    t5.regularhoursofoperation,
    CASE
      WHEN t4.council_district > 20 THEN 'Upper-numbered district'
      WHEN t4.council_district > 10 THEN 'Mid-numbered district'
      ELSE 'Lower-numbered district'
    END as category,
    t2.ownercity
  FROM "Bikes in Buildings Requests_bike_parking_requests_2" t1
  INNER JOIN "Bikes in Buildings Requests_bike_parking_requests_1" t2 ON t1.requestid = t2.requestid
  INNER JOIN "Bikes in Buildings Requests_bike_access_requests" t3 ON t1.indexnumber = t3.indexnumber

I'd like to see the inspection date, E. coli results, biological growth findings, rodent/bird contamination results, the lab that performed the inspection, and whether it meets standards, along with both rank and dense rank values for tracking purposes. The query should join data across multiple tables using bin, block, latitude/longitude, and inspection date as join keys.

WITH ranked AS (
  SELECT 
    t1.latitude,
    t1.inspection_date,
    t5.ecoli,
    t5.si_result_biological_growth,
    t3.si_result_rodent_bird,
    t1.lab_name,
    t4.meet_standards,
    RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY t1.latitude ORDER BY t1.inspection_date DESC) as rank,
    DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY t1.latitude ORDER BY t1.inspection_date ASC) as dense_rank,
    t2.longitude 
    FROM "Self-Reported Drinking Water Tank Inspection Results_drinking_water_tank_inspections_1" t1
  INNER JOIN "Self-Reported Drinking Water Tank Inspection Results_drinking_water_tank_inspections_2" t3

  INNER JOIN "Self-Reported Drinking Water Tank Inspection Results_drinking_water_tank_inspections" t5
    ON t1.block = t5.block
  INNER JOIN "node_2" t2
    ON t1.latitude = t2.latitude AND t1.longitude = t2.longitude
  INNER JOIN "Self-Reported Drinking Water Tank Inspection Results_drinking_water_tank_inspections_3" t4
    ON t1.inspection_date = t4.inspection_date
)
SELECT 
  latitude,
  inspection_date,
  ecoli,
  si_result_biological_growth,
  si_result_rodent_bird,
  lab_name,
  meet_standards,
  rank,
  dense_rank
FROM ranked
WHERE rank <= 1

Zoning Application Portal (ZAP) - Projec.query: Using the Zoning Application Portal (ZAP) Project Data, could you categorize zoning projects by their environmental milestone timing: 'Recent Activity' (after 2023), 'Pandemic Era' (2020-2023), and 'Pre-2020'? For each category, grouped by CEQR type, lead agency, flood zone designations (both A and Shaded X), and actions, please show the count of projects along with the earliest and latest milestone dates.
Zoning Application Portal (ZAP) - Projec.sql:
WITH categorized_data AS (
SELECT 
    t1.ceqr_type, 
    t1.current_envmilestone, 
    t2.ceqr_number, 
    t2.current_envmilestone_date, 
    t5.ceqr_leadagency, 
    t5.flood_zone_a, 
    t4.flood_zone_shadedx, 
    CASE 
        WHEN t2.current_envmilestone_date > '2023-01-01' THEN 'Recent Activity' 
        WHEN t2.current_envmilestone_date > '2020-01-01' THEN 'Pandemic Era' 
        ELSE 'Pre-2020' 
    END as category,
    t6.actions 
    FROM "Zoning Application Portal (ZAP) - Project Data_zoning_application_projects_1" t1
  INNER JOIN "Zoning Application Portal (ZAP) - Project Data_zoning_project_applications" t5
    ON t1.primary_applicant = t5.primary_applicant
  INNER JOIN "Zoning Application Portal (ZAP) - Project Data_zoning_project_milestones" t2
    ON t1.project_id = t2.project_id
  INNER JOIN "Zoning Application Portal (ZAP) - Project Data_zoning_application_projects" t4
    ON t1.ulurp_numbers = t4.ulurp_numbers
  INNER JOIN "node_6" t6
    ON t2.ceqr_number = t6.ceqr_number 
WHERE 
    t1.ceqr_type IS NOT NULL
) 
SELECT 
    ceqr_type, 
    ceqr_leadagency, 
    flood_zone_a, 
    flood_zone_shadedx, 
    category, 
    COUNT(*) as count, MAX(current_envmilestone_date) as max_date, MIN(current_envmilestone_date) as min_date 
FROM 
    categorized_data 
GROUP BY 
    ceqr_type, 
    ceqr_leadagency, 
    flood_zone_a, 
    flood_zone_shadedx, 
    category, actions

Annual Overweight Load (AOL) Permits.query: Using the Annual Overweight Load (AOL) Permits data, could you categorize vehicles by their manufacturer GVWR into 'Light Duty' (≤50,000 lbs), 'Medium Duty' (50,001–80,000 lbs), and 'Heavy Duty' (>80,000 lbs)? For each category, grouped by make, model, and vehicle type, please show the count, average GVWR, total GVWR, and maximum GVWR.
Annual Overweight Load (AOL) Permits.sql:
WITH categorized_data AS (
SELECT 
    t4.manufacturergvwr, 
    t4.registeredgvwr, 
    t1.steeringweight, 
    t2.axle2weight, 
    t5.axle3weight, 
    t2.totalnoofaxle, 
    t5.wheelbase, 
    t2.overalllength, 
    t3.make, 
    t5.model, 
    t2.vehicletype,
    CASE 
        WHEN t4.manufacturergvwr > 80000 THEN 'Heavy Duty' 
        WHEN t4.manufacturergvwr > 50000 THEN 'Medium Duty' 
        ELSE 'Light Duty' 
    END as category 
FROM "Annual Overweight Load (AOL) Permits_overweight_load_permits_2" t1
  INNER JOIN "Annual Overweight Load (AOL) Permits_overweight_load_permits" t3
    ON t1.fullpermitno = t3.fullpermitno
  INNER JOIN "Annual Overweight Load (AOL) Permits_overweight_load_permits_4" t2
    ON t1.permitid = t2.permitid
  INNER JOIN "Annual Overweight Load (AOL) Permits_overweight_load_permits_3" t4
    ON t2.fullapplicationno = t4.fullapplicationno
  INNER JOIN "Annual Overweight Load (AOL) Permits_overweight_load_permits_1" t5
    ON t4.oldpermitno = t5.oldpermitno 
WHERE t3.make IS NOT NULL
) 
SELECT 
    make, 
    model, 
    vehicletype, 
    category, 
    COUNT(*) as count, 
    AVG(manufacturergvwr) as avg_value, 
    SUM(manufacturergvwr) as total_value, 
    MAX(manufacturergvwr) as max_value 
FROM categorized_data 
GROUP BY 
    make, 
    model, 
    vehicletype, 
    category

Vision Zero Base Report.query: Using the Vision Zero Base Report data, for each industry sector, could you identify the top 5 companies with the highest percentage of hybrid or alternative fuel vehicles in their fleet? Please include all their top vehicle models (models 1, 2, 3, 4, and 5), average vehicle age, and longitude coordinates so I can understand the fleet composition and geographic location of the leading sustainable transportation providers.
Vision Zero Base Report.sql:
WITH ranked_data AS (
    SELECT 
        t1.top_vehicle_models_1,
        t1.top_vehicle_models_5,
        t1.average_vehicle_age,
        t2.top_vehicle_models_2,
        t2.percent_hybrid_alt_fuel_vehicles,
        t3.top_vehicle_models_3,
        t3.top_vehicle_models_4,
        t5.industry_sector, 
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
            PARTITION BY t5.industry_sector 
            ORDER BY t2.percent_hybrid_alt_fuel_vehicles DESC
        ) as row_num,
    t4.longitude 
    FROM "Vision Zero Base Report_vehicle_safety_statistics" t1
  INNER JOIN "node_3" t3
    ON t1.phone = t3.phone
  INNER JOIN "Vision Zero Base Report_taxi_base_safety_data" t2
    ON t1.license_number = t2.license_number
  INNER JOIN "Vision Zero Base Report_vehicle_safety_and_accessibility_data" t4
    ON t2.location = t4.location
  INNER JOIN "Vision Zero Base Report_vehicle_safety_reports" t5
    ON t4.latitude = t5.latitude AND t4.longitude = t5.longitude 
    WHERE 
        t5.industry_sector IS NOT NULL
) 
SELECT 
    top_vehicle_models_1,
    top_vehicle_models_5,
    average_vehicle_age,
    top_vehicle_models_2,
    percent_hybrid_alt_fuel_vehicles,
    top_vehicle_models_3,
    top_vehicle_models_4,
    industry_sector 
FROM 
    ranked_data 
WHERE 
    row_num <= 5

Vision Zero Base Report.query: Can you show me, for each taxi base name and its broader business category, how many deadly crashes they've been involved in overall, what the typical number looks like on average, how many individual records that's based on, along with the average vehicle age, vehicle safety technology used, and longitude?

Vision Zero Base Report.query: Could you show me a list of the top industry sectors with the highest number of deadly crashes, including which part of the transportation industry they fall into, what kind of business name they operate under, whether they offer trips that have to be booked in advance rather than hailed on the spot, the total fatal crashes, how many records are in each group, the average fatal crashes, the average vehicle age, and the longitude?

Vision Zero Base Report.query: For Vision Zero Base Report taxi base safety data, show for each group with at least five records that share the same fleet license number in the vehicle safety statistics and taxi base safety data tables, the same phone number in the vehicle safety statistics and node 3 tables, the same percent hybrid or alternative fuel vehicles value, and the same longitude values from both the vehicle safety and accessibility data and vehicle safety reports tables (where these tables are joined through location and latitude/longitude coordinates respectively), display the license numbers from both tables, the phone numbers from both tables, the percent hybrid or alternative fuel vehicles value, how many records there are, along with the total, average, maximum, and minimum of the hybrid or alternative fuel vehicle percentage for that group, but only for records where the hybrid or alternative fuel vehicle share is not missing.
Vision Zero Base Report.sql:
WITH base_data AS (
SELECT t1.license_number AS t1_license_number,
       t2.license_number AS t2_license_number,
       t1.phone AS t1_phone,
       t3.phone AS t3_phone,
       t1.average_vehicle_age,
       t2.percent_hybrid_alt_fuel_vehicles,
       t3.fatal_crashes, t4.longitude, t5.longitude
FROM `Vision Zero Base Report_vehicle_safety_statistics` t1
INNER JOIN `Vision Zero Base Report_taxi_base_safety_data` t2 ON t1.license_number = t2.license_number
INNER JOIN `node_3` t3 ON t1.phone = t3.phone
INNER JOIN `Vision Zero Base Report_vehicle_safety_and_accessibility_data` t4 ON t2.location = t4.location
INNER JOIN `Vision Zero Base Report_vehicle_safety_reports` t5 ON t4.latitude = t5.latitude AND t4.longitude = t5.longitude
WHERE t2.percent_hybrid_alt_fuel_vehicles IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT t1_license_number,
       t2_license_number,
       t1_phone,
       t3_phone,
       percent_hybrid_alt_fuel_vehicles,
       COUNT(*) as record_count,
       SUM(percent_hybrid_alt_fuel_vehicles) as total_amount,
       AVG(percent_hybrid_alt_fuel_vehicles) as avg_amount,
       MAX(percent_hybrid_alt_fuel_vehicles) as max_amount,
       MIN(percent_hybrid_alt_fuel_vehicles) as min_amount
FROM base_data
GROUP BY t1_license_number,
         t2_license_number,
         t1_phone,
         t3_phone,
         percent_hybrid_alt_fuel_vehicles, longitude, longitude
HAVING COUNT(*) >= 5

Vision Zero Base Report.query: For each type of taxi or transportation business, can you show me the top five locations with the highest number of deadly accidents, along with how many safety violations they have per vehicle, how that compares to the typical violation rate for that type of business, what kind of industry they're in, the coordinates for where those places are, the average age of their vehicles, and what vehicle safety technology they use?
Vision Zero Base Report.sql:
WITH ranked AS (
  SELECT 
    t3.fatal_crashes,
    t4.vehicle_safety_violations_per_vehicle,
    t5.sector_average_base_safety_violations_per_vehicle,
    t5.industry_sector,
    t5.latitude,
    t4.longitude,
    t5.longitude,
    t4.latitude,
    RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY t5.industry_sector ORDER BY t3.fatal_crashes DESC) AS rank,

  FROM `Vision Zero Base Report_vehicle_safety_statistics` t1
  INNER JOIN `Vision Zero Base Report_taxi_base_safety_data` t2 ON t1.license_number = t2.license_number
  INNER JOIN `node_3` t3 ON t1.phone = t3.phone
  INNER JOIN `Vision Zero Base Report_vehicle_safety_and_accessibility_data` t4 ON t2.location = t4.location
  INNER JOIN `Vision Zero Base Report_vehicle_safety_reports` t5 ON t4.latitude = t5.latitude AND t4.longitude = t5.longitude
)
SELECT 
  fatal_crashes,
  vehicle_safety_violations_per_vehicle,
  sector_average_base_safety_violations_per_vehicle,
  industry_sector,
  latitude,
  longitude, average_vehicle_age, vehicle_safety_technology_used

Vision Zero Base Report.query: For each taxi base location and matched safety report location in the Vision Zero Base Report, show the number of records, and the average, total, and highest number of fatal crashes, grouped by location, report location, latitude, longitude, industry sector, risk category, and average vehicle age. Also include the risk category (low, medium, or high) based on whether fatal crashes are zero, between one and five, or greater than five, using only records where the industry sector is specified.
Vision Zero Base Report.sql:
WITH categorized_data AS (
  SELECT 
    t2.location,
    t3.fatal_crashes,
    t4.location AS t4_location,
    t4.latitude,
    t4.longitude,
    t5.latitude,
    t5.longitude,
    t5.industry_sector,
    CASE 
      WHEN t3.fatal_crashes > 5 THEN 'high'
      WHEN t3.fatal_crashes > 0 THEN 'medium'
      ELSE 'low'
    END AS category, t1.average_vehicle_age
  FROM `Vision Zero Base Report_vehicle_safety_statistics` t1
  INNER JOIN `Vision Zero Base Report_taxi_base_safety_data` t2 ON t1.license_number = t2.license_number
  INNER JOIN `node_3` t3 ON t1.phone = t3.phone
  INNER JOIN `Vision Zero Base Report_vehicle_safety_and_accessibility_data` t4 ON t2.location = t4.location
  INNER JOIN `Vision Zero Base Report_vehicle_safety_reports` t5 ON t4.latitude = t5.latitude AND t4.longitude = t5.longitude
  WHERE t5.industry_sector IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT 
  location,
  t4_location,
  latitude,
  longitude,
  industry_sector,
  category,
  COUNT(*) AS count,
  AVG(fatal_crashes) AS avg_value,
  SUM(fatal_crashes) AS total_value,
  MAX(fatal_crashes) AS max_value
FROM categorized_data
GROUP BY 
  location,
  t4_location,
  latitude,
  longitude,
  industry_sector,
  category, average_vehicle_age

Property Valuation and Assessment Data.query: Using the Property Valuation and Assessment Data, could you categorize properties by their total assessed value into 'High Value' (>$1,000,000), 'Medium Value' ($500,000–$1,000,000), and 'Low Value' (<$500,000)? For each value category, grouped by borough, tax class, and valuation type, please show the count of records, total assessed value, average value, maximum value, and minimum value, but only include groups with at least 10 records.
Property Valuation and Assessment Data.sql:
WITH categorized_data AS (
  SELECT 
    t1.block, 
    t3.taxclass, 
    t4.stories, 
    t5.borough, 
    t5.avtot2, 
    CASE 
      WHEN t5.avtot2 > 1000000 THEN 'High Value' 
      WHEN t5.avtot2 > 500000 THEN 'Medium Value' 
      ELSE 'Low Value' 
    END as category,
    t2.valtype 
  FROM "Property Valuation and Assessment Data_property_valuation_records" t1
  INNER JOIN "Property Valuation and Assessment Data_property_assessment_records" t2
    ON t1.bble = t2.bble
  INNER JOIN "Property Valuation and Assessment Data_property_tax_assessment" t3
    ON t1.block = t3.block
  INNER JOIN "Property Valuation and Assessment Data_property_valuation_records_1" t4
    ON t1.owner = t4.owner
  INNER JOIN "Property Valuation and Assessment Data_property_valuation_records_2" t5
    ON t2.staddr = t5.staddr
  WHERE t5.avtot2 IS NOT NULL
) 
SELECT 
  borough, 
  taxclass, 
  category, 
  COUNT(*) as record_count, 
  SUM(avtot2) as total_value, 
  AVG(avtot2) as avg_value, 
  MAX(avtot2) as max_value, 
  MIN(avtot2) as min_value 
FROM categorized_data 
GROUP BY borough, taxclass, category, valtype 
HAVING COUNT(*) >= 10
ORDER BY record_count DESC

Property Valuation and Assessment Data.query: Can you show me, for each property owner, their top three years with the highest total assessed value, including the type of tax category they fall under, whether they received any special exemption, the owner's name, the specific year, the amount of any land-related exemption, the time period the assessment covers, the assessed land value, the overall assessed value for those entries, the total assessed value, and the valuation type?

  INNER JOIN `Property Valuation and Assessment Data_property_valuation_records_1` t4 ON t1.owner = t4.owner

INNER JOIN `Property Valuation and Assessment Data_property_assessment_records` t2 ON t1.bble = t2.bble

Property Valuation and Assessment Data.query: Could you show me the top 100 properties, ordered by the highest total assessed value, including the street address, an additional street address field, the type of assessment, the tax class, who owns the property, the time period the assessment covers, the total assessed amount, the count of records, both the average assessed amount for that period and the average total value, but only where the total value is greater than zero?
Property Valuation and Assessment Data.sql:
WITH base_data AS (
  SELECT 
    t2.staddr,
    t2.valtype,
    t2.ext,
    t3.taxclass,
    t4.owner,
    t5.staddr AS t5_staddr,
    t5.period,
    t5.extot, t1.avtot
  FROM `Property Valuation and Assessment Data_property_valuation_records` t1
  INNER JOIN `Property Valuation and Assessment Data_property_assessment_records` t2 ON t1.bble = t2.bble
  INNER JOIN `Property Valuation and Assessment Data_property_tax_assessment` t3 ON t1.block = t3.block
  INNER JOIN `Property Valuation and Assessment Data_property_valuation_records_1` t4 ON t1.owner = t4.owner
  INNER JOIN `Property Valuation and Assessment Data_property_valuation_records_2` t5 ON t2.staddr = t5.staddr
  WHERE t5.period IS NOT NULL
),
aggregated AS (
  SELECT 
    staddr,
    t5_staddr,
    valtype,
    taxclass,
    owner,
    period,
    SUM(extot) AS total,
    COUNT(*) AS count,
    AVG(extot) AS average
  FROM base_data
  GROUP BY staddr, t5_staddr, valtype, taxclass, owner, period, avtot
)
SELECT 
  staddr,
  t5_staddr,
  valtype,
  taxclass,
  owner,
  period,
  total,
  count,
  average, avtot
FROM aggregated
WHERE total > 0
ORDER BY total DESC
LIMIT 100

Property Valuation and Assessment Data.sql: SELECT t2.staddr AS fact_column, t3.taxclass, SUM(t3.excd1) AS total_dimension1, AVG(t4.ltdepth) AS average_dimension2, t4.owner, t5.staddr, t5.avland, t5.period, t1.avtot FROM `Property Valuation and Assessment Data_property_valuation_records` t1 INNER JOIN `Property Valuation and Assessment Data_property_assessment_records` t2 ON t1.bble = t2.bble INNER JOIN `Property Valuation and Assessment Data_property_tax_assessment` t3 ON t1.block = t3.block INNER JOIN `Property Valuation and Assessment Data_property_valuation_records_1` t4 ON t1.owner = t4.owner INNER JOIN `Property Valuation and Assessment Data_property_valuation_records_2` t5 ON t2.staddr = t5.staddr GROUP BY t2.staddr, t3.taxclass, t4.owner, t5.staddr, t5.avland, t5.period, avtot

Over Dimensional Vehicle Permits (ODVP).query: Using the Over Dimensional Vehicle Permits data, could you categorize vehicles by their total gross weight into 'Heavy' (>100,000 lbs), 'Medium' (80,001–100,000 lbs), and 'Standard' (≤80,000 lbs)? For each weight category, grouped by truck registration state, route start state, route end state, and axle 10 weight, please show the count of permits, average weight, total weight, and maximum weight.
Over Dimensional Vehicle Permits (ODVP).sql:
WITH categorized_data AS (
    SELECT 
        t1.loadwidth,
        t1.loadweight,
        t1.truckstate,
        t3.overallheight,
        t3.totalgrossweight,
        t4.wheelbase,
        t4.startstate,
        t4.endstate,
        t5.overallwidth,
        t5.loadheight,
        CASE 
            WHEN t3.totalgrossweight > 100000 THEN 'Heavy' 
            WHEN t3.totalgrossweight > 80000 THEN 'Medium' 
            ELSE 'Standard' 
        END as category,
    t2.axle10weight 
    FROM "Over Dimensional Vehicle Permits (ODVP)_vehicle_permit_details" t1
  INNER JOIN "Over Dimensional Vehicle Permits (ODVP)_vehicle_permit_details_2" t3
    ON t1.fullpermitno = t3.fullpermitno
  INNER JOIN "Over Dimensional Vehicle Permits (ODVP)_vehicle_permit_details_3" t2
    ON t1.permitid = t2.permitid
  INNER JOIN "Over Dimensional Vehicle Permits (ODVP)_vehicle_permit_details_1" t4
    ON t2.fullapplicationno = t4.fullapplicationno
  INNER JOIN "node_5" t5
    ON t4.applicationdate = t5.applicationdate 
    WHERE t3.totalgrossweight IS NOT NULL
) 
SELECT 
    truckstate,
    startstate,
    endstate,
    category,
    COUNT(*) as count, 
    AVG(totalgrossweight) as avg_value, 
    SUM(totalgrossweight) as total_value, 
    MAX(totalgrossweight) as max_value 
FROM categorized_data 
GROUP BY 
    truckstate,
    startstate,
    endstate,
    category, axle10weight

Over Dimensional Vehicle Permits (ODVP).query: Could you show me, for each permit number, how many trips fall into each weight category (Standard, Heavy, Very Heavy), along with the average, total, and maximum overall vehicle weight for those trips, grouped by axle 10 weight and wheelbase, but only for permits where the vehicle was wider than 8 feet?
Over Dimensional Vehicle Permits (ODVP).sql:
WITH categorized_data AS (
  SELECT t1.fullpermitno, t3.fullpermitno, t1.loadweight, t3.totalgrossweight, t5.overallwidth,
         CASE
           WHEN t3.totalgrossweight > 160000 THEN 'Very Heavy'
           WHEN t3.totalgrossweight > 120000 THEN 'Heavy'
           ELSE 'Standard'
         END AS category, t2.axle10weight, t4.wheelbase
  FROM `Over Dimensional Vehicle Permits (ODVP)_vehicle_permit_details` t1
  INNER JOIN `Over Dimensional Vehicle Permits (ODVP)_vehicle_permit_details_3` t2 ON t1.permitid = t2.permitid
  INNER JOIN `Over Dimensional Vehicle Permits (ODVP)_vehicle_permit_details_2` t3 ON t1.fullpermitno = t3.fullpermitno
  INNER JOIN `Over Dimensional Vehicle Permits (ODVP)_vehicle_permit_details_1` t4 ON t2.fullapplicationno = t4.fullapplicationno
  INNER JOIN `node_5` t5 ON t4.applicationdate = t5.applicationdate
  WHERE t5.overallwidth > 8.0
)
SELECT fullpermitno, category, COUNT(*) AS count,
       AVG(totalgrossweight) AS avg_value,
       SUM(totalgrossweight) AS total_value,
       MAX(totalgrossweight) AS max_value
FROM categorized_data
GROUP BY fullpermitno, category, axle10weight, wheelbase

Over Dimensional Vehicle Permits (ODVP).query: Could you show me a breakdown of the total combined vehicle weight for each destination city, along with the axle 6 weight, axle 10 weight, and wheelbase, grouped by the destination city, axle 6 weight, axle 10 weight, and wheelbase, so I can see the weight distribution and vehicle specifications for each city?

INNER JOIN `Over Dimensional Vehicle Permits (ODVP)_vehicle_permit_details_3` t2 ON t1.permitid = t2.permitid
INNER JOIN `Over Dimensional Vehicle Permits (ODVP)_vehicle_permit_details_2` t3 ON t1.fullpermitno = t3.fullpermitno
INNER JOIN `Over Dimensional Vehicle Permits (ODVP)_vehicle_permit_details_1` t4 ON t2.fullapplicationno = t4.fullapplicationno
INNER JOIN `node_5` t5 ON t4.applicationdate = t5.applicationdate GROUP BY t5.endcity, axle6weight, axle10weight, wheelbase

Over Dimensional Vehicle Permits (ODVP).query: Can you show me the top five permits in each trailer's home state with the greatest vehicle width, including where each trip ended (city and ZIP), where it started (state and ZIP), when the permit was applied for, how old the truck was at the time, the axle 6 weight, the axle 10 weight, and how they stack up against others both within the trailer's state and the starting state?
Over Dimensional Vehicle Permits (ODVP).sql:
WITH ranked AS (
  SELECT 
    t3.trailerstate,
    t3.endzipcode,
    t3.truckyear,
    t4.applicationdate,
    t4.startzipcode,
    t4.startstate,
    t5.applicationdate,
    t5.endcity,
    t5.overallwidth,
    RANK() OVER (
      PARTITION BY t3.trailerstate 
      ORDER BY t5.overallwidth DESC
    ) AS rank,
    DENSE_RANK() OVER (
      PARTITION BY t4.startstate 
      ORDER BY t3.truckyear
    ) AS dense_rank, t1.axle6weight, t2.axle10weight
  FROM `Over Dimensional Vehicle Permits (ODVP)_vehicle_permit_details` t1
  INNER JOIN `Over Dimensional Vehicle Permits (ODVP)_vehicle_permit_details_3` t2 ON t1.permitid = t2.permitid
  INNER JOIN `Over Dimensional Vehicle Permits (ODVP)_vehicle_permit_details_2` t3 ON t1.fullpermitno = t3.fullpermitno
  INNER JOIN `Over Dimensional Vehicle Permits (ODVP)_vehicle_permit_details_1` t4 ON t2.fullapplicationno = t4.fullapplicationno
  INNER JOIN `node_5` t5 ON t4.applicationdate = t5.applicationdate
)
SELECT 
  trailerstate,
  endzipcode,
  truckyear,
  applicationdate,
  startzipcode,
  startstate,
  endcity,
  overallwidth,
  rank,
  dense_rank, axle6weight, axle10weight
FROM ranked
WHERE rank <= 5

Over Dimensional Vehicle Permits (ODVP).query: Can you show me, for each combination of application dates from two sources, the state where the trailer is registered, the total gross weight, the length of the load, the overall width, the combined height of all loads, the axle 6 weight, and the axle 10 weight?

INNER JOIN `Over Dimensional Vehicle Permits (ODVP)_vehicle_permit_details_3` t2 ON t1.permitid = t2.permitid
INNER JOIN `Over Dimensional Vehicle Permits (ODVP)_vehicle_permit_details_2` t3 ON t1.fullpermitno = t3.fullpermitno

Over Dimensional Vehicle Permits (ODVP).query: Can you show me the most recent five permits issued since the start of 2023, including the permit number, the dates they were applied for, the permit number from the second details table, the application date from node 5, how heavy the load was, the total weight of the vehicle plus the load, the length and height of the load, the city where each trip was supposed to end, and the weight on axle 10?

Over Dimensional Vehicle Permits (ODVP).query: Could you pull a list of each permit application, showing how many permits are tied to it, when it was submitted, what state the trailer was registered in, which city the trip ended in, and the axle 6 weight?
Over Dimensional Vehicle Permits (ODVP).sql:
SELECT t4.fullapplicationno AS fact_column, COUNT(t2.fullapplicationno) AS permit_count, t4.applicationdate AS application_date, t3.trailerstate AS trailer_state, t5.endcity AS end_city, t1.axle6weight FROM `Over Dimensional Vehicle Permits (ODVP)_vehicle_permit_details` t1
INNER JOIN `Over Dimensional Vehicle Permits (ODVP)_vehicle_permit_details_3` t2 ON t1.permitid = t2.permitid
INNER JOIN `Over Dimensional Vehicle Permits (ODVP)_vehicle_permit_details_2` t3 ON t1.fullpermitno = t3.fullpermitno
INNER JOIN `Over Dimensional Vehicle Permits (ODVP)_vehicle_permit_details_1` t4 ON t2.fullapplicationno = t4.fullapplicationno
INNER JOIN `node_5` t5 ON t4.applicationdate = t5.applicationdate GROUP BY t4.fullapplicationno, t4.applicationdate, t3.trailerstate, t5.endcity, axle6weight

Over Dimensional Vehicle Permits (ODVP).query: Could you pull a list of the top 100 city and state combinations for oversize vehicle permits issued since the start of 2023, showing how many permits went through each city, the total combined width of those loads, and the average width per permit?
Over Dimensional Vehicle Permits (ODVP).sql:
WITH base_data AS (
SELECT 
  t1.permitid,
  t1.fullpermitno,
  t2.permitid AS t2_permitid,
  t2.fullapplicationno,
  t4.fullapplicationno AS t4_fullapplicationno,
  t4.applicationdate,
  t3.fullpermitno AS t3_fullpermitno,
  t3.trailerstate,
  t5.applicationdate,
  t5.endcity,
  t5.overallwidth
FROM `Over Dimensional Vehicle Permits (ODVP)_vehicle_permit_details` t1
INNER JOIN `Over Dimensional Vehicle Permits (ODVP)_vehicle_permit_details_3` t2 ON t1.permitid = t2.permitid
INNER JOIN `Over Dimensional Vehicle Permits (ODVP)_vehicle_permit_details_2` t3 ON t1.fullpermitno = t3.fullpermitno
INNER JOIN `Over Dimensional Vehicle Permits (ODVP)_vehicle_permit_details_1` t4 ON t2.fullapplicationno = t4.fullapplicationno
INNER JOIN `node_5` t5 ON t4.applicationdate = t5.applicationdate
WHERE t5.applicationdate >= '2023-01-01') ,
aggregated AS (
  SELECT 
    trailerstate,
    endcity,
    SUM(overallwidth) AS total,
    COUNT(*) AS count,
    AVG(overallwidth) AS average
  FROM base_data
  GROUP BY trailerstate, endcity
)
SELECT 
  trailerstate,
  endcity,
  total,
  count,
  average
FROM aggregated
WHERE count >= 1
ORDER BY total DESC
LIMIT 100

2017 DOE High School Directory.query: Using the 2017 DOE High School Directory data, could you show me the top 50 schools with the highest total graduation rates? For each school, I'd like to see their DBN, school name, programs, areas of interest (interest1 and interest2), academic opportunities (academicopportunities1 and academicopportunities2), attendance rate, early college options, requirement6_1, along with the total graduation rate, count of records, and average graduation rate across all their programs.
2017 DOE High School Directory.sql:
WITH base_data AS (
    SELECT 
        t1.dbn, 
        t1.school_name, 
        t1.graduation_rate, 
        t1.program1, 
        t2.interest1, 
        t2.academicopportunities2, 
        t5.attendance_rate, 
        t5.earlycollege, 
        t6.academicopportunities1, 
        t6.interest2,
    t3.requirement6_1 
    FROM "2017 DOE High School Directory_high_school_directory_2017" t1
  INNER JOIN "2017 DOE High School Directory_high_school_directory_2017_1" t3
    ON t1.school_name = t3.school_name
  INNER JOIN "node_2" t2
    ON t1.dbn = t2.dbn
  INNER JOIN "2017 DOE High School Directory_high_school_directory_2017_2" t5
    ON t2.phone_number = t5.phone_number
  INNER JOIN "2017 DOE High School Directory_high_school_programs_info" t6
    ON t5.code1 = t6.code1 
    WHERE t1.graduation_rate IS NOT NULL
), 
aggregated AS (
    SELECT 
        dbn, 
        school_name, 
        program1, 
        interest1, 
        academicopportunities2, 
        attendance_rate, 
        earlycollege, 
        academicopportunities1, 
        interest2, 
        SUM(graduation_rate) as total, 
        COUNT(*) as count, 
        AVG(graduation_rate) as average,
    requirement6_1 
    FROM base_data 
    GROUP BY 
        dbn, 
        school_name, 
        program1, 
        interest1, 
        academicopportunities2, 
        attendance_rate, 
        earlycollege, 
        academicopportunities1, 
        interest2, requirement6_1
) 
SELECT 
    dbn, 
    school_name, 
    program1, 
    interest1, 
    academicopportunities2, 
    attendance_rate, 
    earlycollege, 
    academicopportunities1, 
    interest2, 
    total, 
    count, 
    average,
  requirement6_1 
FROM aggregated 
WHERE average > 0 
ORDER BY total DESC 
LIMIT 50

Energy and Water Data Disclosure for Loc.query: Using the Energy and Water Data Disclosure for Local Law 84 2017 (Data for Calendar Year 2016), could you please show me how each property's energy performance compares to national benchmarks? For each address, I'd like to see the variance from national medians, the national median source energy, the adjusted source EUI, along with the total count of records and the sum of adjusted source energy use.
query_related_table: Energy and Water Data Disclosure for Local Law 84 2017 (Data for Calendar Year 2016)_energy_water_usage_2016
Energy and Water Data Disclosure for Local Law 84 2017 (Data for Calendar Year 2016)_nyc_energy_water_disclosure
Energy and Water Data Disclosure for Local Law 84 2017 (Data for Calendar Year 2016)_nyc_energy_water_usage_2016
Energy and Water Data Disclosure for Local Law 84 2017 (Data for Calendar Year 2016)_nyc_energy_water_usage_2016_1
Energy and Water Data Disclosure for Loc.sql:
WITH base_data AS (
  SELECT 
    t1.property_id, 
    t1.address_1, 
    t1.difference_from_national_2, 
    t2.difference_from_national_3, 
    t2.national_median_source_energy, 
    t3.source_energy_use_adjusted, 
    t4.source_eui_adjusted_to_current
  FROM "Energy and Water Data Disclosure for Local Law 84 2017 (Data for Calendar Year 2016)_nyc_energy_water_usage_2016_1" t1
  INNER JOIN "Energy and Water Data Disclosure for Local Law 84 2017 (Data for Calendar Year 2016)_nyc_energy_water_usage_2016" t2
    ON t1.property_id = t2.property_id
  INNER JOIN "Energy and Water Data Disclosure for Local Law 84 2017 (Data for Calendar Year 2016)_nyc_energy_water_disclosure" t3
    ON t1.property_name = t3.property_name
  INNER JOIN "Energy and Water Data Disclosure for Local Law 84 2017 (Data for Calendar Year 2016)_energy_water_usage_2016" t4
    ON t1.address_1 = t4.address_1
  WHERE t1.property_id IS NOT NULL
) 
SELECT 
  address_1, 
  difference_from_national_2, 
  difference_from_national_3, 
  national_median_source_energy, 
  source_eui_adjusted_to_current, 
  COUNT(*) as total_count, 
  SUM(TRY_CAST(source_energy_use_adjusted AS DOUBLE)) as total_amount 
FROM base_data 
GROUP BY 
  address_1, 
  difference_from_national_2, 
  difference_from_national_3, 
  national_median_source_energy, 
  source_eui_adjusted_to_current

NYC Wi-Fi Hotspot Locations.query: Using the NYC Wi-Fi Hotspot Locations data, could you categorize the hotspots by their DOITT ID into three batches: 'Low_ID_Batch' (≤1000), 'Medium_ID_Batch' (1001–2000), and 'High_ID_Batch' (>2000)? For each category, grouped by provider, type, location type, and longitude, please show the count of hotspots along with the average, total, and maximum DOITT ID values, filtering out records where provider is null.
NYC Wi-Fi Hotspot Locations.sql:
WITH categorized_data AS (
SELECT t1.doitt_id, t3.type, t5.remarks, t1.provider, t4.location_t, 
CASE 
    WHEN t1.doitt_id > 2000 THEN 'High_ID_Batch' 
    WHEN t1.doitt_id > 1000 THEN 'Medium_ID_Batch' 
    ELSE 'Low_ID_Batch' 
END as category,
    t2.longitude 
FROM "NYC Wi-Fi Hotspot Locations_nyc_wifi_hotspots_2" t1
  INNER JOIN "NYC Wi-Fi Hotspot Locations_nyc_wifi_hotspots_1" t3
    ON t1.doitt_id = t3.doitt_id
  INNER JOIN "NYC Wi-Fi Hotspot Locations_nyc_wifi_hotspots" t2
    ON t1.objectid = t2.objectid
  INNER JOIN "NYC Wi-Fi Hotspot Locations_nyc_wifi_hotspots_locations" t4
    ON t2.latitude = t4.latitude AND t2.longitude = t4.longitude
  INNER JOIN "NYC Wi-Fi Hotspot Locations_nyc_wifi_hotspots_3" t5
    ON t4.location = t5.location 
WHERE t1.provider IS NOT NULL
) 
SELECT provider, type, location_t, category, 
COUNT(*) as count, 
AVG(doitt_id) as avg_value, 
SUM(doitt_id) as total_value, 
MAX(doitt_id) as max_value 
FROM categorized_data 
GROUP BY provider, type, location_t, category, longitude

NYC Wi-Fi Hotspot Locations.query: Could you give me a breakdown of all Wi‑Fi hotspots activated on September 9th, 9999, grouped by provider, hotspot type, neighborhood code, and density category (categorized as high density for over 40 connections, medium density for 20-40 connections, or low density for under 20), showing the count of hotspots, average connection count, total connections, and maximum connections for each combination?
NYC Wi-Fi Hotspot Locations.sql:
WITH categorized_data AS (SELECT t1.doitt_id, t3.doitt_id, t1.provider, t1.activated, t3.type, t3.coundist, t5.ntacode, t5.remarks, CASE WHEN t3.coundist > 40 THEN 'high density' WHEN t3.coundist > 20 THEN 'medium density' ELSE 'low density' END as category, t2.longitude, t4.longitude FROM `NYC Wi-Fi Hotspot Locations_nyc_wifi_hotspots_2` t1
INNER JOIN `NYC Wi-Fi Hotspot Locations_nyc_wifi_hotspots` t2 ON t1.objectid = t2.objectid
INNER JOIN `NYC Wi-Fi Hotspot Locations_nyc_wifi_hotspots_1` t3 ON t1.doitt_id = t3.doitt_id
INNER JOIN `NYC Wi-Fi Hotspot Locations_nyc_wifi_hotspots_locations` t4 ON t2.latitude = t4.latitude AND t2.longitude = t4.longitude
INNER JOIN `NYC Wi-Fi Hotspot Locations_nyc_wifi_hotspots_3` t5 ON t4.location = t5.location WHERE t1.activated = '9999-09-09T00:00:00.000') SELECT provider, type, ntacode, category, COUNT(*) as count, AVG(coundist) as avg_value, SUM(coundist) as total_value, MAX(coundist) as max_value FROM categorized_data GROUP BY provider, type, ntacode, category, longitude, longitude

NYC Wi-Fi Hotspot Locations.query: Could you show me, for each neighborhood, the top 5 Wi‑Fi hotspot spots ranked by highest nearby user counts, including what kind of hotspot each one is, the user count itself, a clear description of where it's located, any 2010 area or census code tied to that place, another location reference, the neighborhood identifier, any notes or comments recorded about those locations, the ranking position within each neighborhood, a dense ranking by census code within each hotspot type, the property identifier (BBL), and the longitude coordinate?
NYC Wi-Fi Hotspot Locations.sql:
WITH ranked AS (
  SELECT t3.type, t3.coundist, t4.location, t4.bctcb2010, t5.location AS location_t5, t5.ntacode, t5.remarks,
         RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY t5.ntacode ORDER BY t3.coundist DESC) AS rank,
         DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY t3.type ORDER BY t4.bctcb2010) AS dense_rank, t1.bbl, t2.longitude
  FROM `NYC Wi-Fi Hotspot Locations_nyc_wifi_hotspots_2` t1
  INNER JOIN `NYC Wi-Fi Hotspot Locations_nyc_wifi_hotspots` t2 ON t1.objectid = t2.objectid
  INNER JOIN `NYC Wi-Fi Hotspot Locations_nyc_wifi_hotspots_1` t3 ON t1.doitt_id = t3.doitt_id
  INNER JOIN `NYC Wi-Fi Hotspot Locations_nyc_wifi_hotspots_locations` t4 ON t2.latitude = t4.latitude AND t2.longitude = t4.longitude
  INNER JOIN `NYC Wi-Fi Hotspot Locations_nyc_wifi_hotspots_3` t5 ON t4.location = t5.location
)
SELECT type, coundist, location, bctcb2010, location_t5, ntacode, remarks, rank, dense_rank, bbl, longitude
FROM ranked
WHERE rank <= 5

OpenData_ParksProperties.query: Using the NYC Parks Properties data, could you please analyze park properties by their category type, subcategory, community board, and global ID, showing the object ID, property ID, GIS object ID, acquisition method, and retirement status? For each grouping, I would like to see the record count, total acreage, average size, and the range (minimum and maximum) of property sizes, filtered to include only properties with acreage greater than zero and groups with at least one record.
OpenData_ParksProperties.sql:
WITH base_data AS (
    SELECT 
        t3.objectid,
        t3.acres,
        t3.typecatego,
        t4.omppropid,
        t4.subcategor,
        t5.gisobjid,
        t5.acquisitio,
        t5.retired,
    t1.communityb,
    t2.global_id 
    FROM "OpenData_ParksProperties_park_property_details_1" t1
  INNER JOIN "OpenData_ParksProperties_nyc_park_properties" t3
    ON t1.objectid = t3.objectid
  INNER JOIN "OpenData_ParksProperties_park_properties_details" t2
    ON t1.gispropnum = t2.gispropnum
  INNER JOIN "OpenData_ParksProperties_parks_property_details" t4
    ON t1.omppropid = t4.omppropid
  INNER JOIN "OpenData_ParksProperties_park_property_details" t5
    ON t2.gisobjid = t5.gisobjid
    WHERE t3.acres > 0
)
SELECT 
    objectid,
    typecatego,
    omppropid,
    subcategor,
    gisobjid,
    acquisitio,
    retired,
    COUNT(*) as record_count, 
    SUM(acres) as total_amount, 
    AVG(acres) as avg_amount, 
    MAX(acres) as max_amount, 
    MIN(acres) as min_amount
FROM base_data 
GROUP BY 
    objectid,
    typecatego,
    omppropid,
    subcategor,
    gisobjid,
    acquisitio,
    retired, communityb, global_id
HAVING COUNT(*) >= 1

NYC Women's Resource Network Database.query: Using the NYC Women's Resource Network Database, could you categorize published organizations by their community council district ID into 'Low District ID' (≤15), 'Mid District ID' (16–30), and 'High District ID' (>30)? For each organization name, grouped by their registration status, organization type (business, nonprofit, faith-based, government, or professional association), service description, health service indicator, and domestic violence service indicator, please show the count of records, average community council value, total community council value, and maximum community council value.
NYC Women's Resource Network Database.sql:
WITH categorized_data AS (
    SELECT 
        t1.organizationname,
        t2.is_registered_with_the_attorney_general_s_office,
        t2.business,
        t4.nonprofit,
        t4.faith_based_organization,
        t4.other_government_organization,
        t4.professional_association,
        t4.description,
        CASE 
            WHEN t4.community_council > 30 THEN 'High District ID' 
            WHEN t4.community_council > 15 THEN 'Mid District ID' 
            ELSE 'Low District ID' 
        END as category,
        t4.community_council,
    t3.health,
    t5.domestic_violence
    FROM "NYC Women's Resource Network Database_nyc_womens_services_info" t1
  INNER JOIN "NYC Women's Resource Network Database_nyc_womens_organizations_info" t2
    ON t1.organizationname = t2.organizationname
  INNER JOIN "NYC Women's Resource Network Database_nyc_womens_resources" t3
    ON t1.address1 = t3.address1
  INNER JOIN "NYC Women's Resource Network Database_nyc_womens_resources_1" t4
    ON t1.phone = t4.phone
  INNER JOIN "NYC Women's Resource Network Database_nyc_womens_services_locations" t5
    ON t2.location_1 = t5.location_1 
    WHERE t4.published = 'Published'
)
SELECT 
    organizationname,
    is_registered_with_the_attorney_general_s_office,
    business,
    nonprofit,
    faith_based_organization,
    other_government_organization,
    professional_association,
    description,
    category,
    COUNT(*) as count,
    AVG(community_council) as avg_value,
    SUM(community_council) as total_value,
    MAX(community_council) as max_value
FROM categorized_data
GROUP BY 
    organizationname,
    is_registered_with_the_attorney_general_s_office,
    business,
    nonprofit,
    faith_based_organization,
    other_government_organization,
    professional_association,
    description,
    category, health, domestic_violence

DOF： Cooperative Comparable Rental Incom.query: Could you show me, for each Bronx co-op property, where it's located (its coordinates and street address), how much income it's estimated to bring in overall, how much that works out to per square foot for the first comparable rental, and how these properties are categorized into low, medium, or high-income groups along with how many fall into each group and the average, total, and highest estimated income in each category at that address, grouped by the first comparable rental's gross income per square foot?
DOF： Cooperative Comparable Rental Incom.sql:
WITH categorized_data AS (
  SELECT 
    t1.latitude,
    t1.longitude,
    t1.bronx_cooperatives_comparable_properties_address,
    t3.bronx_cooperatives_comparable_properties_address AS t3_bronx_coop_address,
    t4.latitude AS t4_latitude,
    t4.longitude AS t4_longitude,
    t3.bronx_cooperatives_comparable_properties_est_gross_income,
    t4.bronx_cooperatives_comparable_properties_gross_income_per_sqft,
    t5.comparable_rental_1_gross_income_per_sqft,
    CASE
      WHEN t3.bronx_cooperatives_comparable_properties_est_gross_income > 2000000 THEN 'high income'
      WHEN t3.bronx_cooperatives_comparable_properties_est_gross_income > 1000000 THEN 'medium income'
      ELSE 'low income'
    END AS category, t2.comparable_rental_1_gross_income_per_sqft
  FROM `DOF： Cooperative Comparable Rental Income – Bronx – FY 2008 2009_bronx_coop_rental_comparables` t1
  INNER JOIN `DOF： Cooperative Comparable Rental Income – Bronx – FY 2008 2009_bronx_coop_rental_income` t2 
    ON t1.bronx_cooperatives_comparable_properties_boro_block_lot = t2.bronx_cooperatives_comparable_properties_boro_block_lot
  INNER JOIN `DOF： Cooperative Comparable Rental Income – Bronx – FY 2008 2009_bronx_coop_rental_comparisons` t3 
    ON t1.bronx_cooperatives_comparable_properties_address = t3.bronx_cooperatives_comparable_properties_address
  INNER JOIN `DOF： Cooperative Comparable Rental Income – Bronx – FY 2008 2009_bronx_rental_income_comparisons` t4 
    ON t1.latitude = t4.latitude AND t1.longitude = t4.longitude
  INNER JOIN `DOF： Cooperative Comparable Rental Income – Bronx – FY 2008 2009_bronx_coop_rental_income` t5 
    ON t2.bin = t5.bin
  WHERE t3.bronx_cooperatives_comparable_properties_est_gross_income IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT 
  bronx_cooperatives_comparable_properties_address,
  category,
  COUNT(*) AS count,
  AVG(bronx_cooperatives_comparable_properties_est_gross_income) AS avg_value,
  SUM(bronx_cooperatives_comparable_properties_est_gross_income) AS total_value,
  MAX(bronx_cooperatives_comparable_properties_est_gross_income) AS max_value
FROM categorized_data

  category, comparable_rental_1_gross_income_per_sqft

2019 - 2020 School Locations.sql:
WITH base_data AS (    SELECT         t3.administrative_district_name,        t2.location_type_description,        (2020 - CAST(SUBSTR(CAST(t5.open_date AS VARCHAR), 1, 4) AS INTEGER)) as school_age,
    t1.location_name    FROM "2019 - 2020 School Locations_school_locations_2019_2020" t1
  INNER JOIN "2019 - 2020 School Locations_school_location_details" t3
    ON t1.location_code = t3.location_code
  INNER JOIN "2019 - 2020 School Locations_school_location_details_2" t2
    ON t1.system_code = t2.system_code
  INNER JOIN "2019 - 2020 School Locations_school_location_details_3" t5
    ON t2.beds = t5.beds    WHERE         t5.open_date IS NOT NULL         AND t3.administrative_district_name IS NOT NULL), aggregated AS (    SELECT         administrative_district_name,         location_type_description,         SUM(school_age) as total,         COUNT(*) as count,         AVG(school_age) as average,
    location_name     FROM base_data     GROUP BY administrative_district_name, location_type_description, location_name) SELECT     administrative_district_name,     location_type_description,     total,     count,     average,
  location_name FROM aggregated WHERE count >= 3 ORDER BY average DESC LIMIT 20;

Affordable Housing Production by Buildin.query: For each building location, classify its size (Small ≤50, Medium 51-100, Large >100), Construction Type, and Prevailing Wage Status. Then, group these locations by longitude and neighborhood tabulation area to calculate the count of records, total extremely low-income units, average project size, and maximum project size for each category.
Affordable Housing Production by Buildin.sql:
WITH categorized_data AS (    SELECT         t5.reporting_construction_type,        t3.prevailing_wage_status,        t5.total_units,        t2.extremely_low_income_units,        CASE             WHEN t5.total_units > 100 THEN 'Large (>100)'             WHEN t5.total_units > 50 THEN 'Medium (51-100)'             ELSE 'Small (<=50)'         END as category,
    t1.longitude,
    t4.neighborhood_tabulation_area     FROM "Affordable Housing Production by Building_affordable_housing_building_data_1" t1
  INNER JOIN "Affordable Housing Production by Building_affordable_housing_building_data" t3
    ON t1.latitude = t3.latitude AND t1.longitude = t3.longitude
  INNER JOIN "Affordable Housing Production by Building_affordable_housing_units_by_building" t2
    ON t1.building_id = t2.building_id
  INNER JOIN "Affordable Housing Production by Building_affordable_housing_buildings_1" t4
    ON t2.house_number = t4.house_number
  INNER JOIN "Affordable Housing Production by Building_affordable_housing_buildings" t5
    ON t4.project_id = t5.project_id    WHERE         t5.total_units IS NOT NULL         AND t5.reporting_construction_type IS NOT NULL)SELECT     reporting_construction_type,     prevailing_wage_status,     category,     COUNT(*) as count,     AVG(total_units) as avg_project_size,     SUM(extremely_low_income_units) as total_eli_units,     MAX(total_units) as max_size FROM categorized_data GROUP BY     reporting_construction_type,     prevailing_wage_status,     category, longitude, neighborhood_tabulation_area;

Affordable Housing Production by Buildin.query: Can you show me, for the most recent five buildings in each project, the project name, when the building was finished, how many apartments it has in total, how many of those are two‑bedroom units, how many are reserved for middle‑income households and for any other income levels, along with an indication of whether the construction used prevailing-wage labor, as well as the longitude, counted homeownership units, and neighborhood tabulation area?

INNER JOIN `Affordable Housing Production by Building_affordable_housing_buildings` t5 ON t4.project_id = t5.project_id

Affordable Housing Production by Buildin.query: Could you show me, for each building location (latitude and longitude), how many properties fall into each size group (large, medium, or small based on total units), along with the average, total, and largest number of total units at that spot, broken down by counted homeownership units and neighborhood tabulation area, especially focusing on places where the main counted units are available and comparing them with the units reserved for other income levels?
Affordable Housing Production by Buildin.sql:
WITH categorized_data AS (
  SELECT 
    t1.latitude, 
    t1.longitude, 
    t3.latitude AS t3_latitude, 
    t3.longitude AS t3_longitude, 
    t1.all_counted_units, 
    t3.other_income_units, 
    t5.total_units,
    CASE 
      WHEN t5.total_units > 100 THEN 'large'
      WHEN t5.total_units > 50 THEN 'medium'
      ELSE 'small'
    END AS category, t2.counted_homeownership_units, t4.neighborhood_tabulation_area
  FROM `Affordable Housing Production by Building_affordable_housing_building_data_1` t1
  INNER JOIN `Affordable Housing Production by Building_affordable_housing_units_by_building` t2 ON t1.building_id = t2.building_id
  INNER JOIN `Affordable Housing Production by Building_affordable_housing_building_data` t3 ON t1.latitude = t3.latitude AND t1.longitude = t3.longitude
  INNER JOIN `Affordable Housing Production by Building_affordable_housing_buildings_1` t4 ON t2.house_number = t4.house_number
  INNER JOIN `Affordable Housing Production by Building_affordable_housing_buildings` t5 ON t4.project_id = t5.project_id
  WHERE t1.all_counted_units IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT 
  t1_latitude AS latitude,
  t1_longitude AS longitude,
  category,
  COUNT(*) AS count,
  AVG(total_units) AS avg_value,
  SUM(total_units) AS total_value,
  MAX(total_units) AS max_value
FROM (
  SELECT 
    latitude AS t1_latitude,
    longitude AS t1_longitude,
    t3_latitude,
    t3_longitude,
    all_counted_units,
    other_income_units,
    total_units,
    category, counted_homeownership_units, neighborhood_tabulation_area
  FROM categorized_data
) AS categorized_data
GROUP BY t1_latitude, t1_longitude, category, counted_homeownership_units, neighborhood_tabulation_area

Street Construction Permits (2022-Presen.query: Could you break down, for each borough and permit series short description, how many Street Construction Permits (from the 2022–Present records) fall into small (≤100 linear feet), medium (100-500 linear feet), and large (>500 linear feet) projects based on the length of the work area in linear feet, and for each of those size groups show the count, average, total, and maximum project length? Street Construction Permits (2022-Presen.sql:
WITH categorized_data AS (
  SELECT 
    t4.permitissuedate,
    t4.applicationtrackingid,
    t2.permitissuedate AS t2_permitissuedate,
    t5.applicationtrackingid AS t5_applicationtrackingid,
    t3.permitnumberofzones,
    t5.permitlinearfeet,
    t5.boroughname,

      WHEN t5.permitlinearfeet > 500 THEN 'Large'

      ELSE 'Small'

  FROM `Street Construction Permits (2022-Present)_1` t1
  INNER JOIN `Street Construction Permits (2022-Present)_2` t2 ON t1.permitnumber = t2.permitnumber
  INNER JOIN `Street Construction Permits (2022-Present)_3` t3 ON t1.createdon = t3.createdon
  INNER JOIN `Street Construction Permits (2022-Present)_4` t4 ON t2.permitissuedate = t4.permitissuedate
  INNER JOIN `Street Construction Permits (2022-Present)_5` t5 ON t4.applicationtrackingid = t5.applicationtrackingid
  WHERE t5.boroughname IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT 
  boroughname,
  category,
  COUNT(*) AS count,
  AVG(permitlinearfeet) AS avg_value,
  SUM(permitlinearfeet) AS total_value,
  MAX(permitlinearfeet) AS max_value
FROM categorized_data
GROUP BY boroughname, category, permitseriesshortdesc

For each application, list the Object ID, Global ID, Business Address, Legal Name, DBA Name, alcohol qualification, the total roadway area, and BIN.
Open Restaurant Applications (Historic).sql:
WITH base_data AS (    SELECT         t1.objectid,        t1.globalid,        t1.business_address,        t2.legal_business_name,        t3.doing_business_as_dba,        t4.qualify_alcohol,        t2.roadway_dimensions_area,
    t5.bin    FROM "Open Restaurant Applications (Historic)_restaurant_application_records" t1
  INNER JOIN "Open Restaurant Applications (Historic)_restaurant_open_applications" t3

  INNER JOIN "Open Restaurant Applications (Historic)_restaurant_permit_applications" t2

  INNER JOIN "Open Restaurant Applications (Historic)_restaurant_seating_applications" t5
    ON t2.legal_business_name = t5.legal_business_name    WHERE         t2.roadway_dimensions_area IS NOT NULL         AND t1.objectid IS NOT NULL), aggregated AS (    SELECT         objectid,        globalid,        business_address,        legal_business_name,        doing_business_as_dba,         qualify_alcohol,         SUM(roadway_dimensions_area) as total_area,
    bin     FROM base_data     GROUP BY         objectid,        globalid,        business_address,        legal_business_name,        doing_business_as_dba,         qualify_alcohol, bin) SELECT     objectid,    globalid,    business_address,    legal_business_name,    doing_business_as_dba,     qualify_alcohol,     total_area,

DOF： Condominium comparable rental incom.query: Using the Manhattan Condo Rental Income data (FY 2010-2011), let's find the best investment spots. Can you calculate the rental yield (Income / Market Value) for each property? Then, group them by Neighborhood and Building Class. I want to classify them into High (>5%), Medium (3-5%), and Low (<3%) yield categories, and see the count and average yield for each group.
query_related_table: DOF： Condominium comparable rental income – Manhattan - FY 2010 2011_manhattan_condo_rental_comparables
DOF： Condominium comparable rental income – Manhattan - FY 2010 2011_manhattan_condo_rental_comparables_1

DOF： Condominium comparable rental incom.sql:
WITH categorized_data AS (    SELECT         t2.manhattan_condominium_property_neighborhood,        t6.manhattan_condominium_property_building_classification,        t1.manhattan_condominium_property_est_gross_income,        t4.manhattan_condominium_property_full_market_value,        (t1.manhattan_condominium_property_est_gross_income * 1.0 / t4.manhattan_condominium_property_full_market_value) as rental_yield,        CASE             WHEN (t1.manhattan_condominium_property_est_gross_income * 1.0 / t4.manhattan_condominium_property_full_market_value) > 0.05 THEN 'High Yield (>5%)'             WHEN (t1.manhattan_condominium_property_est_gross_income * 1.0 / t4.manhattan_condominium_property_full_market_value) > 0.03 THEN 'Medium Yield (3-5%)'             ELSE 'Low Yield (<3%)'         END as category     FROM "DOF： Condominium comparable rental income – Manhattan - FY 2010 2011_manhattan_condo_rental_comparables_2" t1
  INNER JOIN "DOF： Condominium comparable rental income – Manhattan - FY 2010 2011_manhattan_condo_rental_comparables" t2
    ON t1.manhattan_condominium_property_condo_section = t2.manhattan_condominium_property_condo_section
  INNER JOIN "DOF： Condominium comparable rental income – Manhattan - FY 2010 2011_manhattan_condo_rental_income" t4
    ON t1.manhattan_condominium_property_boro_block_lot = t4.manhattan_condominium_property_boro_block_lot
  INNER JOIN "DOF： Condominium comparable rental income – Manhattan - FY 2010 2011_manhattan_condo_rental_comparables_1" t6
    ON t2.bin = t6.bin    WHERE         t1.manhattan_condominium_property_est_gross_income > 0         AND t4.manhattan_condominium_property_full_market_value > 0)SELECT     manhattan_condominium_property_neighborhood,    manhattan_condominium_property_building_classification,    category,     COUNT(*) as count,     AVG(rental_yield) as avg_value,     SUM(manhattan_condominium_property_est_gross_income) as total_value,     MAX(rental_yield) as max_value FROM categorized_data GROUP BY     manhattan_condominium_property_neighborhood,    manhattan_condominium_property_building_classification,    category;

2018 DOE High School Directory.query: Let's drill down to the neighborhood level using the 2018 DOE High School data. Can you list the top 100 specific schools (by DBN and Name) and their admissions methods within each Neighborhood? I want to see the count of programs they offer and their average Graduation Rate, sorted by the highest graduation rates first in descending order.
2018 DOE High School Directory.sql:
WITH base_data AS (    SELECT         t1.dbn,        t1.school_name,        t5.neighborhood,        t2.method1,        t1.graduation_rate,        t6.college_career_rate    FROM "2018 DOE High School Directory_high_school_directory_2018" t1
  INNER JOIN "2018 DOE High School Directory_high_school_programs" t2
    ON t1.dbn = t2.dbn
  INNER JOIN "2018 DOE High School Directory_high_school_programs_info_2" t5
    ON t2.phone_number = t5.phone_number
  INNER JOIN "2018 DOE High School Directory_high_school_programs_info_1" t6
    ON t2.code1 = t6.code1
  WHERE         t1.graduation_rate IS NOT NULL         AND t5.neighborhood IS NOT NULL), aggregated AS (    SELECT         dbn,        school_name,        neighborhood,         method1,         SUM(graduation_rate) as total_rate_sum,         COUNT(*) as program_count,                      AVG(graduation_rate) as average_graduation_rate     FROM base_data     GROUP BY         dbn,        school_name,        neighborhood,         method1) SELECT     dbn,    school_name,    neighborhood,    method1,    program_count,    average_graduation_rate,    total_rate_sum as total FROM aggregated WHERE average_graduation_rate > 0 ORDER BY average_graduation_rate DESC LIMIT 100;

2018 DOE High School Directory.query: Show about 20 high schools from the 2018 DOE High School Directory with the highest average college and career readiness rate, including each school's name from both t1 and t3 tables, fax number from both t1 and t4 tables, borough, the total average college and career readiness rate, count of records, the average rate, and grade 9 GE applicants per seat, ranked from highest to lowest on that readiness rate.
2018 DOE High School Directory.sql:
WITH base_data AS (
SELECT t1.school_name AS t1_school_name,
       t1.fax_number AS t1_fax_number,
       t3.school_name AS t3_school_name,
       t4.fax_number AS t4_fax_number,
       t3.attendance_rate,
       t4.pct_stu_safe,
       t5.boro,
       t6.college_career_rate, t2.grade9geapplicantsperseat1
FROM `2018 DOE High School Directory_high_school_directory_2018` t1
INNER JOIN `2018 DOE High School Directory_high_school_programs` t2 ON t1.dbn = t2.dbn
INNER JOIN `node_3` t3 ON t1.school_name = t3.school_name
INNER JOIN `2018 DOE High School Directory_high_school_programs_info` t4 ON t1.fax_number = t4.fax_number
INNER JOIN `2018 DOE High School Directory_high_school_programs_info_2` t5 ON t2.phone_number = t5.phone_number
INNER JOIN `2018 DOE High School Directory_high_school_programs_info_1` t6 ON t2.code1 = t6.code1
WHERE t3.attendance_rate IS NOT NULL
  AND t6.college_career_rate IS NOT NULL
),
aggregated AS (
SELECT t1_school_name,
       t1_fax_number,
       t3_school_name,
       t4_fax_number,
       boro,
       AVG(college_career_rate) AS total,
       COUNT(*) AS count,
       AVG(college_career_rate) AS average
FROM base_data
GROUP BY t1_school_name,
         t1_fax_number,
         t3_school_name,
         t4_fax_number,
         boro, grade9geapplicantsperseat1
)
SELECT t1_school_name,
       t1_fax_number,
       t3_school_name,
       t4_fax_number,
       boro,
       total,
       count,
       average, grade9geapplicantsperseat1
FROM aggregated
WHERE total > 0
ORDER BY total DESC
LIMIT 20

    t4.final_spending_deadline    FROM "Use of ARRA Stimulus Funds_arra_stimulus_fund_usage_2" t1
  INNER JOIN "Use of ARRA Stimulus Funds_arra_stimulus_fund_usage_1" t3

  INNER JOIN "Use of ARRA Stimulus Funds_arra_stimulus_payments" t2

  INNER JOIN "Use of ARRA Stimulus Funds_arra_stimulus_fund_projects" t5
    ON t4.contract_name = t5.contract_name    WHERE         t2.payment_value IS NOT NULL         AND t3.funding_category IS NOT NULL)SELECT     funding_category,     payment_type,     COUNT(*) as record_count,     SUM(payment_value) as total_amount,     AVG(payment_value) as avg_amount,     MAX(payment_value) as max_amount,     MIN(payment_value) as min_amount FROM base_data GROUP BY     funding_category,     payment_type, final_spending_deadline HAVING COUNT(*) >= 10;

Parking Violations Issued - Fiscal Year.query: Using the 'Parking Violations Issued - Fiscal Year 2023' dataset, let's track the latest enforcement actions. Can you group the violations by 'Vehicle Make' and identify the 5 most recent tickets for each brand? I want to see the Summons Number, Plate ID, Issue Date, Violation Code, Street Name, and the Issuing Agency.
Parking Violations Issued - Fiscal Year.sql:
WITH ranked_data AS (    SELECT         t1.summons_number,        t1.plate_id,        t3.vehicle_make,        t1.issue_date,        t2.violation_code,        t4.street_name,        t5.issuing_agency,        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (            PARTITION BY t3.vehicle_make             ORDER BY t1.issue_date DESC        ) as row_num     FROM "Parking Violations Issued - Fiscal Year 2023_parking_violations_2023_1" t1
  INNER JOIN "Parking Violations Issued - Fiscal Year 2023_parking_violations_2023" t3
    ON t1.plate_id = t3.plate_id
  INNER JOIN "Parking Violations Issued - Fiscal Year 2023_parking_violations_fy2023" t2
    ON t1.summons_number = t2.summons_number
  INNER JOIN "Parking Violations Issued - Fiscal Year 2023_parking_violations_fy2023_1" t4
    ON t2.street_name = t4.street_name
  INNER JOIN "Parking Violations Issued - Fiscal Year 2023_parking_violation_records_2023" t5
    ON t4.violation_time = t5.violation_time    WHERE         t1.issue_date IS NOT NULL         AND t3.vehicle_make IS NOT NULL) SELECT     summons_number,    plate_id,    vehicle_make,    issue_date,    violation_code,    street_name,    issuing_agency FROM ranked_data WHERE row_num <= 5;

Parking Violations Issued - Fiscal Year.query: Could you pull the most recent ten parking tickets per enforcement team issued by agency "P," and for each one show me which enforcement team wrote it, the specific violation code and its description, the law section and subdivision it falls under, the date it was first observed, which agency actually issued it, the issue date, the vehicle body type, and the plate type?
Parking Violations Issued - Fiscal Year.sql:
WITH ranked_data AS (
SELECT t3.issuer_squad, t3.violation_legal_code, t3.violation_description, t3.law_section, t3.sub_division, t5.date_first_observed, t5.issuing_agency, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY t3.issuer_squad ORDER BY t5.date_first_observed DESC) as row_num, t1.issue_date, t2.vehicle_body_type, t4.plate_type 
FROM `Parking Violations Issued - Fiscal Year 2023_parking_violations_2023_1` t1
INNER JOIN `Parking Violations Issued - Fiscal Year 2023_parking_violations_fy2023` t2 ON t1.summons_number = t2.summons_number
INNER JOIN `Parking Violations Issued - Fiscal Year 2023_parking_violations_2023` t3 ON t1.plate_id = t3.plate_id
INNER JOIN `Parking Violations Issued - Fiscal Year 2023_parking_violations_fy2023_1` t4 ON t2.street_name = t4.street_name
INNER JOIN `Parking Violations Issued - Fiscal Year 2023_parking_violation_records_2023` t5 ON t4.violation_time = t5.violation_time 
WHERE t5.issuing_agency = 'P')
